about: Rows the closure pass judged: options, full card and mechanisms. Built by tools/closure_cards.py from hybrids/A.settled.json and B.settled.json.

cells.why: E-22: 600 of 600 partitions linearizable and every replica equal to the fold of the committed log, but the write p99 bar is not shown on a real kernel (E-02's TS pipeline, 4.3 ms against 5.7 ms, does no protocol work); the native bar (C + 0.5 ms) cannot be settled on this box's one disk; PD's, ISR's and SLOG's shapes were never run; BUY cannot run a seeded sweep. Open for all 18
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Writer time as the median (A-23) expired no row early and copies agreed at each position (E-21, 30 seeds a family; E-22, 100 seeds in 3 modes). Not shown: the O(expired) tick pin at 1e6 rows. The bound is read as writer time while a writer exists; read to the letter, a failover near the ttl made expiry 2,036 ms late, in any one-writer design (the alt). PD's T tso was not modelled by E-21 and its cell is the same
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-31 model-checked subscribe with A-06's END and per-slot cursors on ten bounds (up to 7.6 million states): a snapshot then deltas, no gap, no overlap across a leader crash, a reload, a slot move and a relay. E-22's near-cache check (one-hop miss, shortfall, the memory bound) passed 100 of 100 seeds in 3 modes
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 11)

cells.why: E-22: six readers that miss one key at once make one load, run at the key's writer and filled with if: absent, and a write during the load keeps its value, in 100 of 100 seeds in 3 modes with a leader change and a slot move; the number of readers does not enter the mechanism
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Re-ruled (RR-02): open as worded (E-08's 1.2 ms is one working point; a probe at 0.38 of a core gave 0.79 ms), met as restated. As worded it fails like every row: C + one hop is about 0.83 ms and E-08's relay alone had p99 1.2 ms (Node) at 1,000 subscribers; the gap counts 1.2 against 0.83. Restated with a window per room and about 1,000 sockets a core it is met: per-room order and rooms-only delivery held in E-22, the reconnect cursor holds in E-31's model, and E-08's relay encodes each room once at 0.57 to 1.5 M deliveries a second a core. Per-slot cursors (E-31)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 15)

cells.why: Order and delivery held on both rungs in E-22 (none lost 0 of 900), but no fero kernel has run nats bench against the none rung, core NATS sits only 1.9 times under E-02's socket-free TS ceiling, and the none rung's failover rule was never modelled (K-10). PD's, ISR's, SLOG's and OBJ's shapes were never run either; their cells are the same
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-31 holds the log-reader property (every committed record once, in order) on ten bounds, up to 7.6 million states, across a leader crash, a reload, a slot move and a relay; E-22's stream check resumed from saved cursors and got expired with a readable earliest. LANE: no partition moves, so a lane offset keeps its meaning. SPLIT: E-17b and E-17c model a reader across a split and a merge with 2 to 3 lineage rules. P-07 sets no speed bar: Kafka and Redpanda runs are PERF-05 and PERF-06
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Safety holds on the prototype (nothing skipped, no zombie commit, E-22; exactly once past the horizon with A-05's mark, E-30), but 'a crash hands its partitions on within one lease plus one commit' is neither measured nor held by construction. CELL and SPLIT add that the mark's carry across a re-key or split was not modelled; the families never run and BUY are open too
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22's queue check passed in 100 seeds in 3 modes with a worker killed, a worker paused 40 s and a forced leader change and slot move: each job removed once, dead-letter after 5 deliveries, never two live leases, FIFO first deliveries, an empty take appends nothing (real Knossos agrees, E-22b). A re-key (E-17c) and a split (E-17b) carry the dedup outcomes; P-09 names no move
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22's lock check (holder paused 15 s, clock skewed 3 s, a #locks failover): both fencing checkers clean in every seed; the fence refused every stale write under every clock rule (E-21); the highest token travels in a move, a re-key and a split (E-17, E-17b, E-17c); a restore starts above the store's mark (E-33). Acquire is one conditional write, so one commit
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Exactly once and the bounds hold in E-22's simulation and in E-20's dedup model (sess 13 rules, win 17), but the op cost at the writer (3 µs TS, 0.5 µs native) was never measured on any L2, and memtier INCR has only driven a simulator (PERF-02). Open for all 18
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Merged views equal the query only with data's merge contract (A-10), which is not landed; today group costs O(rows per bucket), 2,574 µs at 1e6 rows against 1 µs (E-05, E-23). 'Every row runs the same data, so no row differs': open for all 20
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22 after A-04 (a session-bound write waits for its session's record): a killed client's rows went on every copy within 9.8 s of a 10 s lease, a client paused 5 s kept its rows, 100 seeds in 3 modes; leases by median writer time pass E-21. Read to the letter, a #sessions failover near the lapse gave 12.4 s (the alt)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: With A-04 all 183,159 partition histories were linearizable in Porcupine and Knossos agrees (E-22b); two sells of the last item gave one ok in all 300 races under leader changes, slot moves and the shuffle, wherever the calls ran (E-22); the ported Raft was linearizable in 26 of 26 Maelstrom runs (E-46)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Re-ruled RR-11 (judging/closure/rerulings.cells.json), on closure referee B's lead: a saga unit that touches a memory-rung resource can be half kept when that group's majority stops uncleanly inside the sync window (its step is lost while the unit is recorded done), and the lost tail can take back the fence raise that stops a paused holder. E-24, the met cell's support, leaves unclean recovery out (K-09, G-05). One stated rule would close it (a saga's writes on a memory resource commit at persisted, or the unit is refused); no row states it, so the cell is open, not a fail. R lists the rows that carry the memory rung (closure/mechanisms.json, memory-rung). Overrides the saga else (met).
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 1)

cells.why: X saga shows half a unit by design: Elle finds fractured reads in 66 to 77 of 100 saga histories even with A-24 (E-22, E-22b). X none (V4) has no unit at all. RAMP would give it for plain sets only, and no row holds X ramp
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22's rebuild check passed and history: 'all' kept every record, but byte for byte fails today for some views: a sum depends on record order (E-43) and top-k breaks ties by arrival (E-23). A-10's contract fixes both but is not landed in data. Every row runs the same data
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-30 model-checked A-05's mark (per consumer, source slot and output slot, written in the output's own entry, carried when the output slot moves): 5 rules, each A record lands in B once even past the dedup horizon and across a B slot move; E-22's derive check gave exact totals with a member killed mid-batch
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 17)

cells.why: TEST-05 and TEST-07 hold on prototypes (E-22, E-06), but TEST-06 is open for every row: the fork was not built, its storage cost was not measured, and a fork that runs costs O(rows). Open for all 20
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-31 model-checked subscribe with A-06's END and per-slot cursors on ten bounds (up to 7.6 million states): a snapshot then deltas, no gap, no overlap across a leader crash, a reload, a slot move and a relay. E-22's near-cache check (one-hop miss, shortfall, the memory bound) passed 100 of 100 seeds in 3 modes. P-19 carries P-03's promises over the same client, so the row's P-03 cell decides

cells.why: Upcasters held in E-22 over three versions with the migrating server killed, but it stays open with P-16 (byte for byte waits on data's contract, A-10), and an old tape replayed on new code was not run
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22's prototype has typed rows, a schema refused at the writer and a re-runnable migration, but 'paced so P-01's p99 holds during a roll' cannot be shown in a simulation with no real clock. SRV (U cli), CELL and SPLIT (the mark's carry) and the families never run are open for more reasons
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: The semantics hold in E-22 (383 answers, 17 timeouts of 400, never two answers), but an ask is three persisted commits, 6.0 ms against two hops; a service on the none rung was not built. Open for all 20
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22: a delayed message never taken early by writer time with the clock skewed 200 ms, a waiting take appends nothing. Not shown: delay counts from the adder's clock (E-22 D5), and the wake pin of C + one hop on a real kernel
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-22's queue keeps one sub-partition per priority level inside a partition and takes the levels in order; the priority-0 message came first in 100 of 100 seeds in 3 modes under faults and the shuffle. A first version, not tuned or timed
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: open for all 20: the floors are measured (C = 0.73 ms, E-01), each competitor ran with its own tool 3 times, and E-45 names a driver for each row, but the gateways only drove a simulator, 6 to 54 times below Redis (E-09a2), so no row is won yet. Wins and losses are scored in PERF-02 to PERF-07.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Redis matched: 91,600 SETs a second, p99 4.9 ms (memtier, E-09a, E-09a2). E-02's pipeline ceilings sit 5 to 60 times above the matched rows and 3 to 5 times above the default rows, so no build is stopped, but no fero kernel ran through the RESP gateway at speed (E-45). The held-row clause holds: 81 ns in process against a 1.26 ms GET (E-44). A row with no `memory` rung meets Redis's default with `persisted`: a thin margin, not a measured loss.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: NATS core here: 2.25 M msgs a second one to one, 4.13 M deliveries a second to 16, p99 0.27 ms (E-09b). E-02's `none` ceiling with no sockets is 4.3 M a second in TS (1.9 times NATS, the thinnest margin) and 18.6 M in Rust; a Node relay pushed 0.57 to 1.50 M deliveries a second per core (E-08). No `none` path ran through `nats bench`, so the row is neither won nor lost.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Q `mix` has a `memory` rung, the matching rung for JetStream's default (p99 0.55 ms). E-02's bare pipeline reads 0.57 ms in TS, a tie, and 0.33 ms in Rust, a win, at 50,000 writes a second and never with one write in flight, so the native step carries the default row; the matched one-publisher row (1.31 ms) is open in both phases (E-09b, E-02).
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 2)

cells.why: Kafka here: matched 86,344 records a second of 1 KiB, default 240,043 (E-09c). E-02's persisted ceiling is 284,000 a second in TS (3.3 times the matched row, only 1.18 times the default) and 349,000 in Rust; E-02 has no 1 KiB `memory` run, and the Kafka gateway has only driven a simulator (E-45).
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: Redpanda here: 175,420 records a second of 1 KiB with an fsync at a majority, p99 43 ms at half rate (E-09d). E-02's persisted ceiling is 1.62 times above it in TS (the thinnest matched margin, with no CPU margin) and 1.99 times in Rust. No fero kernel ran behind the Kafka gateway at speed.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: etcd here: 1,118 puts a second at one client (p99 1.73 ms) and 22,800 at 1,000 clients (E-09e). E-02's ceilings are 40 to 120 times above the throughput rows, but its TS tail (2.4 to 4.3 ms) is above etcd's one-client p99 and Rust's is 1.58 ms, read at 10,000 to 50,000 writes a second, never one in flight. The etcd gateway has only driven a simulator (E-45).
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: TS bar C + 5 ms = 5.7 ms: E-02's bare pipeline reads p99 4.3 ms (3.7 ms with the kernel on a worker), but E-11's real TS Raft on a simple host read 10 to 11 ms at 10,000 writes a second. Native bar 1.23 ms: the Rust pipeline reads 1.58 ms on this one shared disk and 0.67 ms with emulated separate disks; etcd itself reads 1.73 ms. A `ts→rs` row is judged on the TS bar first. ISR's WAL per group is a weak point (p99 9 to 147 ms from 256 groups, E-12) but the pin names no group count; PD's LSM write path was not measured.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-02's bare pipeline commits 2.8 M appends a second in TS (1.53 M with a client front, E-39), 30 to 56 times the TS bars, and 2.2 to 4.1 M in Rust on this disk against 500,000 per process and 2 M per writer; these are ceilings with no Raft core, L2 or fold, and the real TS Raft ran only at 10,000 writes a second (E-11). ISR's file per group reaches 0.29 to 1.27 times the journal's rate (E-12); SLOG's loglet write quorum and OBJ's batching into large PUTs (E-28) were not run.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: one clause is measured: a held-row read costs 81 ns through data (E-44), under 100 ns. The conditional op (3 µs) and the method call at the writer (10 µs) were not timed on any v5 kernel (E-02 spends 0.26 µs per extra append; data's fold 0.22 to 1.90 µs a record, E-05). Where the row holds W `ridx` or `lease`, a `fresh` read is one round and no fsync by construction. U `cli` rows (SRV, PD) have no method-at-the-writer case; SIDE's call to its daemon costs about 33 µs over a socket (E-03), a weak point, not a measured ceiling.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: E-08's one-thread Node relay, which encodes each room's records once and writes that one buffer to every subscriber, pushed 0.57 to 1.50 M deliveries a second per core with no added wait, 6 to 15 times the TS bar, and keeps 0.89 to 0.95 of that over WebSocket (E-40); the Rust relay pushed 11.9 to 13.4 M, 4 times the native bar. For a `ts→rs` row the TS phase carries the verdict. BUY's relay is the NATS server: 2.5 M deliveries per server core-second, each message encoded once.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: with quiet groups (A-12), 2,000 idle groups sent nothing of their own and cost 0.15 % of a core on the TS Raft port, 0.10 % on etcd's raft in Go and 0.04 % on raft-rs (E-11). With one ping per member pair, a Node member with 99 links pinged every 500 ms plus 2,000 quiet groups used 0.95 % of a core (0.33 % in Rust), and n = 100 makes 19,800 frames a second (E-25). It holds, narrowly in TS and only up to n = 100.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 0)

cells.why: no experiment timed retention or compaction per tick. By design retention drops or uploads whole segments, flat by intent, but snapshot layers, their merging and TTL expiry were not priced from 1e3 to 1e7 rows. PD's LSM compacts in the background, work that grows with data written and kept: a weak point, still open.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: a process rule, the same for every row: no pinned quiet runner exists (this box moved up to 36 % between boots, E-09a2), and no v5 pin exists yet; no design stops them.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: judge 2 was right: E-22's prototype found every caught-up replica's rows equal to a fresh fold of the log on every seed, but on one TS thread with rows by value only; views over the same rows (a float `sum`, tie order) differ between a replica that folded every record and one that rebuilt or started from a snapshot until data takes the merge contract (E-23 run B, E-43; A-10). Rows kept off the V8 heap were checked only by E-05's digest. SRV and PD fold natively and need DATA-09's differential test; ISR's Kafka-style transactions make the fold hold records back, not designed; no monitor compares folds on BUY.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: a layering rule no option breaks: one TypeScript module imports data's one entry, and a native server imports none. Checked by search: only proto/seam.ts in E-22's prototype, only buy.mjs in E-44's, and api/substrate.ts in v4 today. The guard test itself is phase-1 work, but it guards a fact the prototypes already show.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: the designs carry data's change records as log entries under a header that wraps them (about 3.9 B a record, E-19), and E-22's prototype folds records verbatim. But the v5 header and codec are phase-1 work: byte values must be allowed (E-45), a view stream may carry data's `move` records (E-22), and a format V8 decodes whole is planned (A-13). No v5 codec has a round-trip test.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: data's debt, the same for every row (A-10): its 18 clauses run in fero's battery today, but two data commits that both say SCHEDULE_VERSION 4 fold differently (E-43), the merge contract (E-23) and a restore rule (E-06) are not written, and the 4 to 5 bump fero needs is not published.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: data's debt, the same for every row: views stay data's operators, but data's `group` rebuilds a touched bucket on each commit (2,574 µs a record at 1e6 rows against 1 µs per affected view, E-05), equal top-k views are not shared, and `top-k` and `sum` need the merge contract (E-23).
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: judge 2 was right: no check in E-22 has user code that throws, and a probe on its prototype let a throwing tap's AggregateError out of the seam into the replica's apply step, and the run stopped. A kernel on its own worker, native core or process cannot be reached by a user throw (E-07), but the Fault path on the thread that folds is not built or tested for v5.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: judge 2 was right: a mutation probe on E-22's prototype broke the rule: after a field-level write, a row read through a `filter` view was not frozen, and writing to it changed what that server held (999 against 5 on the others). The seam freezes rows on `get` and `snapshot` only, so a frozen row on every hand-out path, and its cost against the 100 ns read, is not shown.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: a process rule, the same for every row: fero's CI runs no perf suite today, data's included, because no pinned quiet runner exists; no design stands in the way.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: `ts→rs` rows: in the TS phase nothing is native, and the native step carries the verdict. It either keeps data folding in JS (holds by construction, E-03) or holds rows natively, as DESIGN-V5's native fold would, which needs the differential test; that test was not run (E-43's 1e6-record stream and E-04's state-comparing guard are ready inputs). SRV's and PD's servers fold plain rows natively (PD in a multi-version LSM store), and the test was not run for them either.
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: no v5 stack was timed on example 01. The nearest prototype, E-26's TS Raft host, starts three processes in 265 to 318 ms but holds about 96 MB a process against the 100 MB bar, and quiet groups idle near 0 CPU (E-11). Rows with a native server (H srv, side) work only if npm ships the binary and fero(name) spawns it, and that spawn was not timed (SPACE 4.2)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: every row decides roles by node config, but no v5 example series exists to run at 1, 3 and 5 processes or hosted. E-33 changed the first start across boxes: a conditional create in the object store, or one `fero init`, which both judges call a weak point, not a fail, because the files stay the same. v4's series and BUY's four E-44 patterns were not run as one set at each size either
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3 'SC-10 and SC-03': as worded every design reaches 12 to 22 effective writers under Zipf 0.99, below F_w = 64 (E-18), because nothing splits the hottest partition. Restated with the app split, a slot row states 135 at 4,096 slots, moved one slot at a time by one loop (A-16, A-18; in cent and cent-co rows the mover is the controller, in COMP the loop on #meta's leader). It stays open: 0.7 x n was never run on real processes and the loop saw exact loads (G-32); for `pslot` rows E-18 never balanced many resources in shared groups (K-04), and for COMP the loop never ran beside healing leaders (K-07)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 4)

cells.why: the same slot move that grows a resource empties a group (E-17 `shrink` holds, model-checked, crash-only), and the one-move policy has a margin against flapping (E-18: without it two pieces swapped for ever in 48 of 300 cases); a re-key can go down (E-17), split + merge shrinks (E-17b), v4 leaves by ballot. But no 7-day load cycle was simulated, and nothing ran the rule that decides when to add or drop a group
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3 'SC-05 at 10 GB': one Node process wakes 10 GB of 2 KB rows in 86 to 122 s against 60 s (5 GB in 36 s, E-34). The time is v4's JS crc32c and decode, not the design, and A-13's faster wake is planned and not built, so it is open. Restated per storage form it is still open: no sleep-and-wake test ran against an S3-compatible store, with disks kept or lost
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: by design only: cold rows read through from snapshot layers (opt in), and groups spread a resource over servers (DESIGN-V5 4.1, 'later'). No experiment ran a data set at 3 x RAM, and a cold row cannot be a sync read (X15). V4 spreads a resource by `replicas: N` with no cold rows; it is open too (referee)
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: the idle cost at n = 100 is stated or counted (E-25: 0.95% of a core in Node and 19,800 frames a second with quiet groups for the Raft rows; counts for ISR, SLOG, OBJ), and the knob past 100 is A-12's peer bound. But no v5 kernel ran a sim sweep at n = 100, and E-25 injected no failure
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3 'SC-08(b), every slot row': a three-commit slot move is unwritable 16.7 ms at p99 under 10,000 writes a second against 10 ms; one commit stays at or under 4.7 ms (E-13). A-17 cuts the move to one or two commits, but that cut was never model-checked with unclean recovery (K-03). (a), (d), (f) hold in the move's models (E-15, E-17c) and E-18's run; (c) was never pinned and no sweep ran moves with membership changes (K-01). For OBJ each commit is a PUT (E-28). Restated to a p50 plus a load-tied p99 it is open for the same reasons
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 2)

cells.why: any row can give each limit a health row and a stderr line at 80%, but no row has the warnings built and tested; only E-29's prototype printed its disk line once. No row's design blocks it; v4 as built has none, and BUY's layer could warn only on limits it can read from NATS
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3 'SC-10 and SC-03': as worded the effective writer count is 12 to 22 for every design, below F_w = 64 (E-18). Restated with the app split the stated ceiling is 135 writers at 4,096 slots (72 at 1,024), the E-18 figure under A-18's one-move policy run by the loop or controller; prototypes hold 2,000 groups a process (E-11, E-12) and 100 members (E-25). It stays open: no ceiling is pinned and the price of 4,096 slots is reasoned only (G-06). It also depends on F_w and N_res
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 5)

cells.why: referee: with N `proc` nothing is resident and nothing is sent for a sleeping project (E-26), but the 10% clause rests on a promise: E-35 ran tenants on one disk only (1.20 to 1.36 times even with a journal each) and marks `proc` 'reasoned, not tested', and a cloud volume shared by tenants will not keep them apart (G-17). BUY: tenancy is the outside log's, not tested
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: one Node server held 10,000 idle links in 89 MB at 0.88% of a core, and 1,000 active subscribers at 10 messages a second cost 8.8% of a core (17% over TLS) with p99 2.0 ms (E-27); native edges: E-08's one-thread Rust relay served 1,000 and 10,000 sockets at 13.4 and 11.9 million deliveries a second (the referee gives PD the same as SRV). A-11 puts a TLS terminator in front
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: referee, AMENDMENTS 1.3 'SC-13's small' (pslot too): with a run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state and dormant groups (A-15, A-16) an idle resource measured 1.4 KB at 10 touched slots and 8.8 KB at 100, about 85 B a touched slot (E-36); with `pslot` 0.4 to 1.2 KB at 1 to 10 slots with no dormant groups. The text does not say what 'small' is, so that is no measured ceiling below the bar. Open as worded and restated: the cold-open tail is 5.4 to 7.6 ms against 5 ms, and the drop clauses and the 1e5 create-and-drop sim never ran; `pslot`'s cold open is reasoned and E-36 priced one slot map per project (G-16), a loglet's idle cost (SLOG) and OBJ's create on a store were not measured
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 2)

cells.why: no sim ran with 80 to 150 ms links, so false failover, the lease and TTL checks and the far-read lag bar are unshown. A relay or learner with any delay keeps every subscribe property (E-31, model-checked; lag not modelled), and writer time as the median ran for one group only (E-21). If the user wants writes homed in several regions the bars change, and it stays open
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule else)

cells.why: on the shared journal the ratio was 1.18 and 1.26 times in two sets of runs, against 1.2 (E-35): at the bar. Here groups are shared by many resources, so the big record also sits in the same group's batch as other resources' records, which was never run (K-06); the size limits were not built
cells.source: predicted from the judged rows (rule 0)

cells.why: A persisted write is on disk at a majority of voters before the answer, which is Raft's own commit rule (R raft; RLOG's log group is Raft). TLC on etcd's spec lost no committed entry through crashes and a lost disk replaced under a new id (E-14c), nor with one bad entry under rejoin (E-37). cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. TLC on etcd's own spec, three voters, with one bad entry below the commit point (par1: 62,743 states, complete, 0 of 1,897 judged states stuck; par1r2: 455,856) and with one on each of two replicas (par2d: 565,222; par2: 1,362,748): all 10 invariants hold in every run, NoLostCommit included, so no committed write is lost. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. This row keeps learners. A learner never stands and is no voter of its own configuration, so the three voters' elections are as modelled; par's rule (no vote while an entry is marked) covers a damaged learner too. A learner whose commit index covers the entry is a good repair source by Raft's state machine safety (reasoned). The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not.
cells.j1: met (E-37's par runs; the row must take E-37's form, which refuses its vote while damaged)
cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)
cells.source: closure judges, A.settled.json

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. This row keeps learners. A learner never stands and is no voter of its own configuration, so the three voters' elections are as modelled; par's rule (no vote while an entry is marked) covers a damaged learner too. A learner whose commit index covers the entry is a good repair source by Raft's state machine safety (reasoned). The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. Under the memory rung a replica that stops uncleanly comes back as new by disk-incarnation's rule before par can act; that is the rung's trade, not F-22's case, which asks about fsynced entries. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. TLC on etcd's own spec, three voters, with one bad entry below the commit point (par1: 62,743 states, complete, 0 of 1,897 judged states stuck; par1r2: 455,856) and with one on each of two replicas (par2d: 565,222; par2: 1,362,748): all 10 invariants hold in every run, NoLostCommit included, so no committed write is lost. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not.
cells.j1: met (E-37's par runs; the row must take E-37's form, which refuses its vote while damaged)
cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)
cells.source: closure judges, A.settled.json

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. Under the memory rung a replica that stops uncleanly comes back as new by disk-incarnation's rule before par can act; that is the rung's trade, not F-22's case, which asks about fsynced entries. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

cells.why: Open, as for every Raft row (settled: COMP, MIN-P, SRV, PD; and the two V full rows, ISR and V4). The operator command (DESIGN-V5 4.2: list what may be lost, refuse while a voter it would drop answers, bump the slot epochs, refuse stale cursors) was neither built nor modelled. E-15 keeps the slot move safe through one unclean recovery (up to 7.5 million states) and E-33 refuses a cursor a restore does not hold. No learners, or who issues the command, changes any clause, and no model gives a counterexample. For a par row the command must also cover one more case: a committed entry with no good copy left while both damaged voters still answer (E-37 par2, its 4 stuck states). There it drops no voter; it clears the bad marks and accepts the listed loss, so the 'refuse while a voter it would drop answers' clause is not in its way. That is design work owed (j1's note, accepted), not a proof of failure. C cent: PD's unsafe-recover is the nearest published command; PD's cell is open too.

cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. TLC on etcd's own spec, three voters, with one bad entry below the commit point (par1: 62,743 states, complete, 0 of 1,897 judged states stuck; par1r2: 455,856) and with one on each of two replicas (par2d: 565,222; par2: 1,362,748): all 10 invariants hold in every run, NoLostCommit included, so no committed write is lost. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. With C cent the leader's own links come from link pings, which this row carries (mechanism ruling below), so A-20's re-check still sees the damaged voter as alive.

cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. With C cent the leader's own links come from link pings, which this row carries (mechanism ruling below), so A-20's re-check still sees the damaged voter as alive. Under the memory rung a replica that stops uncleanly comes back as new by disk-incarnation's rule before par can act; that is the rung's trade, not F-22's case, which asks about fsynced entries. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. This row keeps learners. A learner never stands and is no voter of its own configuration, so the three voters' elections are as modelled; par's rule (no vote while an entry is marked) covers a damaged learner too. A learner whose commit index covers the entry is a good repair source by Raft's state machine safety (reasoned). The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not.
cells.j1: met (E-37's par runs; the row must take E-37's form, which refuses its vote while damaged)
cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. This row keeps learners. A learner never stands and is no voter of its own configuration, so the three voters' elections are as modelled; par's rule (no vote while an entry is marked) covers a damaged learner too. A learner whose commit index covers the entry is a good repair source by Raft's state machine safety (reasoned). The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. TLC on etcd's own spec, three voters, with one bad entry below the commit point (par1: 62,743 states, complete, 0 of 1,897 judged states stuck; par1r2: 455,856) and with one on each of two replicas (par2d: 565,222; par2: 1,362,748): all 10 invariants hold in every run, NoLostCommit included, so no committed write is lost. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not.

cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

cells.why: Met in E-37's form of par. TLC on etcd's own spec, three voters, with one bad entry below the commit point (par1: 62,743 states, complete, 0 of 1,897 judged states stuck; par1r2: 455,856) and with one on each of two replicas (par2d: 565,222; par2: 1,362,748): all 10 invariants hold in every run, NoLostCommit included, so no committed write is lost. Each clause of F-22 (M) holds in that form. A checksum marks the entry bad (ParDetect). While it is marked, the replica grants no vote, does not stand and takes no append, so it never votes or acknowledges on it. The vote guard and the stand guard are each shown needed (dropping the first broke MoreUpToDateCorrectInv in 32 states; the second, LogMatchingInv on par2d in 56 states). The append guard is not needed for safety, but F-22's words 'never ... acknowledges on it' ask for it, so the row keeps it. par-repair's record says the replica 'keeps its vote'; read literally that loses a committed write (E-37's vote mutant), so the record must say E-37's form (record fix below). The bound is the one every rejoin row's met cell rests on: three voters, no membership change, damage found at a restart, no damage to the term or vote record. Par with a voter change is owed (G-15; VERDICT section 0 line 7): an open edge, not a counterexample. The card prints rejoin's basis for this rule; for a par row the basis is the par runs above. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. With C cent the leader's own links come from link pings, which this row carries (mechanism ruling below), so A-20's re-check still sees the damaged voter as alive.
cells.j1: met (E-37's par runs; the row must take E-37's form, which refuses its vote while damaged)
cells.j2: met (E-37's par runs; E-37's form, not 'keeps its vote'; three voters, no membership change)

cells.why: Met. With one bad entry on each of two replicas at different offsets, every judged state reaches a working leader with no operator step (E-37 par2d: 565,222 states, complete; 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck; all invariants hold). With the same offset allowed (par2: 1,362,748 states) only 4 of 1,388 judged states are stuck, each a committed entry with no good copy left anywhere: that is F-12's case, and staying unavailable is the right answer. Repair must come from any good peer, as E-37's rule does: repair only from the leader leaves 9 % (par2d-leader, 22 of 244) and 4 % (par2-leader, 54 of 1,292) of those states stuck. The settled F-22 (S) cell of every rejoin row says only Z par keeps the group writable. Not modelled with a voter change, or with damage above the commit point (PAR's 'possibly committed' query; G-15): open edges, not counterexamples. With V full the voters are three per group, the shape E-37 modelled. The only learner is the healer's short catch-up stage (mechanism ruling below), which never stands. The healer cannot spoil the two-damage case (reasoned, both judges): both damaged voters refuse votes, so no leader exists and no command runs until one repair is done; and a removal runs only when the replica is gone on the group leader's own links (A-20, E-16's exec.gone), which a live damaged voter is not. With C cent the leader's own links come from link pings, which this row carries (mechanism ruling below), so A-20's re-check still sees the damaged voter as alive. A repair write is not in A-09's reserve list (E-29), so on a full disk a damaged voter waits for space; F-22's case is unaffected.

The prediction copies PD's cell, which cites Percolator and TiKV: a unit commits at its primary record, and a later reader resolves a dead or paused holder's locks. That promise rests on every participant's locks and commit record being durable. This row adds Q `mix` beside X `2pc`, which no judged row and no cited system holds: a `memory` write commits in memory at a majority, and a majority that stops uncleanly inside the sync window loses it (the settled `memory-rung` unit; AMENDMENTS 2, Q). Now b's half is kept and a's half is gone: half a unit, which P-15 forbids ('never half-forgotten'). The trace is reasoned, not model-checked, and one rule inside the row closes it (a unit that touches a `memory` partition writes its locks and commit record at `persisted`, or is refused), so it is not a fail, and no structural fail is confirmed. But the row states no such rule, and the rung's safety was never modelled (K-09, G-05), so 'met' has no support. cells.why: Open, not met (referee; judge 2's crossing upheld). The prediction copies PD's cell, which cites Percolator and TiKV: a unit commits at its primary record, and a later reader resolves a dead or paused holder's locks. That promise rests on every participant's locks and commit record being durable. This row adds Q `mix` beside X `2pc`, which no judged row and no cited system holds: a `memory` write commits in memory at a majority, and a majority that stops uncleanly inside the sync window loses it (the settled `memory-rung` unit; AMENDMENTS 2, Q). Judge 2's trace, checked here against the units' own rules: (1) a unit writes key a in a `memory` resource, where its primary sits, and key b in a `persisted` one; (2) the primary commits on a's group, and b's lock is committed forward on b's group; (3) a majority of a's group stops uncleanly inside the window, and its replicas come back as new. Now b's half is kept and a's half is gone: half a unit, which P-15 forbids ('never half-forgotten'). The trace is reasoned, not model-checked, and one rule inside the row closes it (a unit that touches a `memory` partition writes its locks and commit record at `persisted`, or is refused), so it is not a fail, and no structural fail is confirmed. But the row states no such rule, and the rung's safety was never modelled (K-09, G-05), so 'met' has no support. Judge 1 named the same interaction in its mechanism review and kept met only because the saga rows with Q `mix` keep met; their cell rests on E-24, which leaves unclean recovery out (K-09). So the same gap sits under COMP, DRAFT, CELL, SPLIT and COMP2: a lead for a re-ruling there, not changed here.
cells.j1: met (kept as predicted; the interaction named in its mechanism review)
cells.source: closure judges, B.settled.json

cells.why: Met, by model, by both judges. Z `par` as E-37 modelled it on etcd's spec: a checksum per entry marks the bad entry; the replica keeps its id, grants no vote, does not stand, and copies the entry from a peer that knows it is committed and whose own copy is good. Run par1 (one damaged entry below the commit point; 62,743 states, complete): all 10 invariants hold and 0 of 1,897 judged states are stuck, so no committed write is lost and the replica never votes on the bad entry; each of par's 7 rules is shown needed by a mutant. The core is the TypeScript port of etcd's raft, which E-37's spec models and which passes all 41 of etcd's datadriven files byte for byte (E-10); par's rules go inside the port. Limits: three voters, one group, no membership change (G-15), while this row's controller heals by member change. LSM form: the Raft log lives in the LSM, so damage comes as a bad block that may hold several entries; the store's block checksum finds it, each entry is repaired from a peer, the bad file is dropped and its rows re-copied by a region snapshot. And one rule: the LSM's WAL recovery must never cut a damaged record below what was acknowledged as a torn tail, which is E-37's 32-state loss (RocksDB's point-in-time recovery mode stops replay at the first bad record; from memory, not checked). These are rules to state, not counterexamples: met, as COMP2's `par` cell (VERDICT section 1).
cells.source: closure judges, B.settled.json

With the same offset bad on two replicas it stays writable whenever a good copy is left (par2: the only 4 stuck states of 1,388 have no good copy anywhere, which is F-12's case). Repair must come from any peer, not only the leader (par2d-leader: 22 of 244, 9 %, stuck). This is the cell VERDICT section 1 gives COMP2 on the same run. Same limits as the MUST: no membership change (G-15), and on an LSM the damage unit is a block, not one entry.

Restated as 'C plus the longest normal gap between commits plus 5 ms' it is open: the port's handover was not timed, and failover at E = 2 s with 0.25 E jitter sums to 2.5 s with no margin (reasoned, not run; at E = 1 s one native failover took 1.42 s against 1.25 s)

This row adds one, behind the local store: writes, elections and new replicas use the local LSM and peers (a new replica copies a snapshot from a peer), and the tier uploads behind them, as ISR's Kafka-style tier does (KIP-405). So a down store should hold back only uploads, sleep, wake and old history, which F-15 allows. Not shown: no sim ran with the store down for an hour (E-33's store is always reachable), and the local disk grows while uploads wait. That is ISR's settled ground, which is open. Form (ruled here): judge 2 added 'open, restated' with depends_on 'restated'; judge 1 gave none. AMENDMENTS 1.3's F-15 line names 'every row that restores by A-08', whose restore mark makes a slot move wait for the store. This row carries no restore mark (the settled count leaves PD out: its tokens are the oracle's timestamps, saved in the controller; MECHANISMS section 4) and has no slot moves, so the line does not reach it. Both readings give open, so the cell carries no alternative. If the oracle's window were ever kept in the store before use (judge 1's proposed unit, not taken below), a store outage longer than the window would stop writes, which F-15 forbids: one more reason to keep it in the controller's own Raft group.

cells.why: Met, by model, by both judges. Z `par` as E-37 modelled it on etcd's spec: a checksum per entry marks the bad entry; the replica keeps its id, grants no vote, does not stand, and copies the entry from a peer that knows it is committed and whose own copy is good. Run par1 (one damaged entry below the commit point; 62,743 states, complete): all 10 invariants hold and 0 of 1,897 judged states are stuck, so no committed write is lost and the replica never votes on the bad entry; each of par's 7 rules is shown needed by a mutant. The core is raft-rs (carried by reasoning, as the settled RUST and SRV cells carry E-37) or etcd's raft in Go (the spec's own code); either needs par's vote and repair rules added inside it, a fork. Limits: three voters, one group, no membership change (G-15), while this row's controller heals by member change. LSM form: the Raft log lives in the LSM, so damage comes as a bad block that may hold several entries; the store's block checksum finds it, each entry is repaired from a peer, the bad file is dropped and its rows re-copied by a region snapshot. And one rule: the LSM's WAL recovery must never cut a damaged record below what was acknowledged as a torn tail, which is E-37's 32-state loss (RocksDB's point-in-time recovery mode stops replay at the first bad record; from memory, not checked). These are rules to state, not counterexamples: met, as COMP2's `par` cell (VERDICT section 1).
cells.source: closure judges, B.settled.json

cells.why: Met, by model, by both judges. Z `par` keeps the group writable with one bad entry on each of two replicas: run par2d, 565,222 states, complete, 276 judged two-damage states, 0 stuck, every invariant held (E-37). With the same offset bad on two replicas it stays writable whenever a good copy is left (par2: the only 4 stuck states of 1,388 have no good copy anywhere, which is F-12's case). Repair must come from any peer, not only the leader (par2d-leader: 22 of 244, 9 %, stuck). This is the cell VERDICT section 1 gives COMP2 on the same run. Same limits as the MUST: no membership change (G-15), and on an LSM the damage unit is a block, not one entry.
cells.source: closure judges, B.settled.json
